title: OCM Cell Composition v1.0
description: The instance layer (ADR-0017): which modules, placed where, wired how, and what the cell reads/records/produces. Authored via ocm-api (ADR-0012); consumed by ocm-resolve, the generator, and the coordinator. Port shape and the ports-vs-subsystem-block split follow ADR-0026.

ocm_version.description: Spec version this cell is written against. cell.py accepts only '1.0' today.

id.description: Reverse-DNS unique identifier for the cell.

base.description: The base module the cell is built on, plus the datum frame and bolt grid everything places against.

controller.description: Which runtime/target/fieldbus the generated coordinator is emitted for.

safety.description: NOT a risk assessment. Hardwired and separately certified; the generator only refuses a build whose declared safety hardware doesn't meet it. `verified_by` is a human signature -- the API refuses to write it (spec/06, OCM_HUMAN_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED).

part.description: The physical part and its named features (e.g. part.features.hole_1) -- the assembly-sequence DSL the planner interprets. Kept opaque here (additionalProperties: true) on purpose: typing it would reach into the planner (cell.py leaves it a raw dict).

plan.description: The assembly plan -- verbs only (ADR-0023 D1). Kept opaque here (items: true) for the same reason as `part`: the planner owns its shape, not this schema.

ports.description: ADR-0026 D1: a cell's external boundary, one entry per connection a net or link can name. Same flat shape as a module port (ADR-0015) -- an identifier, a domain, the domain's descriptor. NO nested signals, NO direction, NO behaviour, and NO `domain: identification` (ADR-0026 D2/D3/D4).

nets.description: ADR-0015/0026: electrical, pneumatic, or safety connectivity as NETS -- N unordered endpoints on a common node. Optional; a cell declaring none stays valid (a single-cell install has no interconnect), mirroring the module layer.

links.description: ADR-0015/0026 (Erratum 1): communication connectivity as LINKS -- exactly two endpoints, each naming a port. Optional. The record_sink is NOT a valid endpoint; it is reached from the traceability port via record_sink.port, not named by a link.

identity.description: ADR-0020 + ADR-0026 D2: reader configuration for part identity at cell entry. A top-level subsystem block, NOT a port -- nothing is netted to a reader; it reads a tag that arrives on a carrier.

reader.description: Resolvable component ref for the reader head.

carriers.description: ADR-0020: carrier fleet declaration and wear budget. Not a boundary object -- a fleet fact.

tag.description: Resolvable component ref for the carrier tag (ADR-0014).

carrier.description: ADR-0031: the cell's carrier instance -- which carrier TYPE (a carriers/ entry) and where it enters. The carrier's kinematic chain is rooted at the LOCATED datum the `located_on` module declares (mechanical.located, D3), never at the mechanism that brings it there: both transit joints at zero IS the located pose, transit is negative offset, and the part datum derives from machined geometry and nothing else (D2). Identity and wear stay ADR-0020's `carriers` block -- a different question about the same object.

instance.description: This cell's own name for the carrier instance (like a module instance name).

located_on.description: The module instance whose mechanical.located datum roots this carrier's chain (D2/D3). The module must declare `located`; a cell naming one that does not refuses at resolve.

entry_mm.description: Where the carrier ENTERS the cell -- the far end of the transit chain, as negative offsets from the located datum (D2: 'travel: -400 mm at the entry opening, lift: -12 mm riding the belt'). Declaring it is what makes the transit joints' range a stated fact rather than a fabrication: the chain's prismatic joints carry limit [entry, 0], where 0 is the hard stop the datum is machined at. OPTIONAL: a cell that never models transit omits it, and the carrier is composed seated (welded) at the located datum. Nothing anywhere declares a COMMANDED travel -- entry is a place, not a target.

transit_mm.description: The carrier's CURRENT offsets from the located datum, if it is mid-transit -- requires entry_mm (the range the values must sit in). OPTIONAL: absent means seated at the located datum, both joints at zero, which is the state the cell's work happens in.

record_sink.description: ADR-0021: where the cell's records drain to. Declared, not wired.

port.description: ADR-0026 Erratum 1: the cell ports[].id this sink drains through (e.g. the traceability communication port). The subsystem block references the port -- a link never names the sink.

produces.description: ADR-0021: what the cell measures and records. Derived from components, not wired.

unit.description: Verbatim unit as the source prints it (ADR-0014 -- never converted, never enum-constrained). Whether `source` can actually produce it is a resolve-time check (OCM_MEASUREMENT_SOURCE_INVALID), not schema.

source.description: Resolvable `instance.component`-style ref that produces this measurement.

type.description: e.g. 'series' for a curve; absent means a scalar.

mode_selector.description: ADR-0024 + ADR-0026 D2: the AUTO/MANUAL/EDIT keyswitch. Wired to this cell's own safety circuit, not across a boundary, so it is a subsystem block, not a port. Declares intent; does not certify the mode (spec/06).

component.description: Resolvable component ref for the keyswitch.

instance_pose.description: An instance's pose relative to the cell's base datum.

module_instance.description: One placed module. `address` is intentionally open (additionalProperties: true) -- its shape varies by protocol, matching InstanceAddress.raw in cell.py.

instance.description: Unique instance name within the cell.

mount.description: Where the instance sits: a grid station + pose, or `on` another instance's flange.

address.description: Fieldbus/network address; known keys lifted, the rest kept verbatim (cell.py InstanceAddress.raw). Open by design.

tool.description: spec/02: which end effector instance is mounted.

joint_state.description: Named joint -> radians, applied when composing the scene.

requires.description: ADR-0023: binds this instance's capability `requires` keys to concrete 'instance.signal' targets. Whether the target exists is a resolve-time concern.

port.description: ADR-0026 D1: a cell boundary endpoint a net/link can name. No signals, no direction, no behaviour.

domain.description: ADR-0026 D2: NO 'identification' -- identity is a top-level block, not a port.

role.description: Boundary role as the design labels it, e.g. 'smema-downstream', 'smema-upstream', 'fsoe-slave'. Open vocabulary -- cell roles are domain-specific and broader than the module comms enum.

endpoint.description: ADR-0015/0026 (Erratum 1): one end of a net or link. Names a cell `port` (+ optional `pin`), or reaches into a contained module via `{instance, port, pin}` (ADR-0026 D3, reference-downward). Nothing else -- a link endpoint naming a non-port is rejected structurally (OCM_LINK_ENDPOINT_NOT_A_PORT, surfacing as OCM_SCHEMA_INVALID). Exactly-one-primary-reference and downward resolution are resolve-time concerns.

instance.description: A modules[].instance, when reaching into that module's own port.

pin.description: A pin on the named port -- resolves downward to a module port (ADR-0026 D3); the cell cannot create a pin.

net.description: ADR-0015: N unordered endpoints on a common node. `active` (ADR-0026 D4) is a design choice declared HERE, on the net -- never on a port or a pin.

active.description: ADR-0026 D4: active state, declared on the net.

link.description: ADR-0015: exactly two endpoints (a cable between two ports, or a port and the record_sink).
